Right then, England are out in the middle, and here come the India openers, Abhishek and Samson. The latter is taking strike, with Archer already at the top of his mark. Slip in

6.53pm: Sun going down over the city, floodlights glaring. Time for the anthems. And time to mention our Live Blog, which is today being helmed by Sid Monga - go show him some love in the emojis

Sid is also our Tactics Board guru, and we're about to get a look at some of the key match-ups: starting with Sanju Samson taking on Jofra Archer, and Abhishek Sharma vs the Will Jacks Offspin Gambit

"SKY always says he wanted to do same what he got after he losses the toss," reckons Sandeep. "Is this some kind of psychology thing."

"After yesterdays blow out, is a close, competitive game in order?" Let's hope it's a doozy, James

6.45pm: Good evening, all. And thanks, Ekanth. The Wankhede is filling up and the atmosphere building. They've flocked along Marine Drive, ready to cheer their heroes to the rafters. Might be a few Barmy Army members in there, too. Have England landed the first blow by winning the toss? We'll soon see, although the suggestion is that dew won't be a big factor tonight

If anyone needs a reminder of what happened the last time these teams played a T20I in Mumbai (and India batted first) - it went pretty well for the home side

Alllright, wait's over, it's time for Alan to raise the temperature here.

Pitch report: Warmer day today. Pitch No. 7, 75 metres straight, 65 metres square of the wicket. Ian Bishop says the ground has been sprayed with anti-dew spray that'll keep dew to a minimum. Ball spun on this surface more than adjacent surfaces - 2.3 degrees - there's more grass on it today. He hopes for a surface full of runs.

India XI: 1 Abhishek Sharma, 2 Sanju Samson (wk), 3 Ishan Kishan, 4 Suryakumar Yadav (capt), 5 Tilak Varma, 6 Hardik Pandya, 7 Shivam Dube, 8 Axar Patel, 9 Arshdeep Singh, 10 Varun Chakravarthy, 11 Jasprit Bumrah

England XI: 1 Phil Salt, 2 Jos Buttler (wk), 3 Jacob Bethell, 4 Harry Brook (capt), 5 Tom Banton, 6 Sam Curran, 7 Will Jacks, 8 Jamie Overton, 9 Liam Dawson, 10 Jofra Archer, 11 Adil Rashid.



Suryakumar Yadav, India captain We'd have batted. Wind around, don't think there'll be dew. Mood in camp is positive. We've tightened our screws, our brand of cricket has been different. Best wicket, credit to the curator and groundsman. Same team

Harry Brook, England captain Looks a good wicket, hope to get a good start and then chase it down. India have a lot more experience, we'll try and assess conditions and play at our best. T20 is fickle, way we've played we've scraped through and holds us in good stead. Overton comes in for Rehan

6:31pm Toss coming up. Ravi Shastri with the captains. Tails is the call from Brook. It is tails, England will bowl

Rohit Sharma gets a good welcome form the Mumbaikars including the North Stand faithful, Nagraj says. Cheers of "Roohit Sharmaa" going on

With ten minutes to go for the toss, Jos Buttler and then Harry Brook address the England huddle. Brendon McCullum nods along, then smiles. Brook says good luck and the huddle breaks. Just Brook in game kit, rest are in training colours.

Analysis from Nagraj Adil Rashid takes it slow and makes batters go oh no

6:20pm England's batting and bowling has been bolstered by Will Jacks' remarkable form. Adil Rashid has also been good, whether the change in conditions from Sri Lanka to India affects him is to be seen. He did bowl well against West Indies at this venue. Then there's Jofra who is ever-reliable in the powerplay and Curran, whose slower ones are hard to hit at the death. Like India, there are no straightforward weaknesses, the question is how many of them can have a good day.




Morkel: 'For Varun, it's just about getting that confidence, and trying not to overthink it'


6:10pm India's bowling is stellar, with Jasprit Bumrah and Arshdeep Singh as the wicket-takers. Hardik Pandya takes the new ball and can bowl in the middle overs too. Varun Chakravarthy is unplayable on his day but has had a couple of bad games. He'll hope to come back strongly. But this is an all-conditions attack.

Arshdeep, Shivam Dube, Varun Chakravarthy, too, have marked their run-ups, Nagraj informs




Tactics board by Sidharth Monga: Archer vs Samson, the best overs for Varun, and the Adil Rashid factor

From Nagraj: It it is interesting to see that the curator has decided to use the light roller with 35 minutes to go for toss. Bumrah is the first Indian to mark his run-up

5:55pm India's top order too has an up-and-down story. Abhishek was on top of the world before the tournament but slumped, Tilak Varma too didn't set things alight and had to slip down the order and make way for Sanju Samson. Samson had the game of his life against West Indies but is still yet to consistently make runs for India. He's best placed to change things tonight. Let's see if he can.




Jamie Overton, the one possible change predicted from the England XI, is taking throwdowns from Ben Duckett. So count him in, Nagraj says. Curran and Archer first ones to measure run-ups. Overton has marked his run-up, he's likely to replace Rehan

5:45pm Both Buttler and Phil Salt have had a rough tournament so far. England will hope they come to form because a launchpad would be perfect for a middle order that's found multiple match-winners so far. On a day where, to use Miller's phraseology, velocity can be traded for volume with regards to run-scoring, a quick start - like NZ showed yesterday, could be match-defining.

Exposition from Nagraj: This match is vital for two individuals in the England camp: Baz McCullum and Jos Buttler, and for different reasons. A positive result matters for McCullum after the Ashes defeat. For Buttler, this is possibly his last World Cup in this format, he needs runs to sign off on a high. The pair were the first to have a look at the pitch from the England camp.

Tim Venner: "Will they be brave enough to drop Buttler (down the order ?), and open with Jacks ?  Alas probably not."

Anand: "Kuldeep should come in, England hasn't picked Kuldeep at all. This again depends on the pitch though."

Nagraj Gollapudi, our correspondent at the Wankhede, has gathered some info - Two days back the pitch, which wore a raw green mango shade, made those on the outside wonder if this would be seamer-friendly track. But the greenish tinge has toned down with more rough around the crease at both ends. The pitch, as noted in our copies, will have good bounce and likely to take lesser turn than the England-West Indies match which was played on the same surface.

Amit: "Hi Eknath do see India bringing Kuldeep yadav in place of Varun or arshdeep? since England has issue against spin earlier?" Nope, think India are going unchanged. What about you?




Match Preview by Andrew Miller: India vs England chapter 3: the match that could define eras

Weather-wise, it's been a hot day. Bright evening right now, no weather interruptions expected. Dew could be an issue.

5:30pm One good day, that's all it takes as New Zealand found out yesterday and these two teams found out in the last two T20 World Cups. England bashed India in the 2022 semi-final, the reverse was true in 2024, what's it going to be this time? Atmosphere-wise, this will be the loudest but potentially the most tense. Could be the same over here. We're looking forward to all the company. Welcome, hope we have a banger.

launched! Is that the sign that Buttler is back? Back of a length outside off and he simply manhandles it over extra cover, sailing all the way. Nonchalant tonkage from England's past-master

brilliantly held running back! Bumrah strikes first ball now. Slower one, completely dupes Brook as he goes hard through the shot. Axar has to run yards and yards back from point, watching the ball drop over his shoulder, and then takes a sprawling catch in front of the packed stands! Superb from Bumrah, matched by his fielder
pre_text: Jasprit Bumrah on now
dismissal: HC Brook c Patel b Bumrah 7 (14m 6b 1x4 0x6) SR: 116.66

commentary: good length on off stump, dabbed to cover
shovelled into the boundary boards! Silence reigns. Length ball on the hip and Bethell just whips it up and over short fine leg
round the wicket, pace off and it deflects off the pads through to Samson
pace off, this spins almosts, through to the keeper over the stumps as Bethell fails to read it
another change-up, 125kph, comes off the body, maybe outside edge as well down to deep third
pre_text: "Brilliant catch!" yelps Jambu. "Heart in the mouth for everyone! Felt eternity from the time ball was hit and landed in Axar's palm"

commentary: hoicked over long-on! Too short from Varun and Bethell, who's had his difficulties against spin, rocks deep to heave a pull for six
pre_text: Varun Chakravarthy is on in the powerplay

commentary: cleaned out once again, floated out full and Bethell steps into a mighty mow down the ground, this one all the way over long-off!
reverse-slogged for six! Goes over the wicket, flicked out on leg stump and Bethell scoops him nonchalantly over deep point! Varun enduring a nightmare start
pushed through, 109kph, much flatter delivery and Bethell taps it for one

bowled him! Buttler's mojo isn't coming back. Flighted googly, 95kph/60mph, hits the top of middle stump as Buttler heaves blindly. Varun smiles, maybe breathes a sigh of relief. This was Buttler's highest score since the opening game against Nepal, but he was nowhere near connecting with a swingeing blow down the ground
gets off the mark with a reverse-swept four! Looped up outside off and he turns around, connects with his pet shot through backward point
pre_text: Tom Banton is next in

commentary: length ball angling across from over the wicket, Bethell looks to reverse-scoop it, but misses
pre_text:
Hardik again, field spread

"With that wicket, do you think it is over for England? There is still hope, if Bethell can keep going." Lloyd Christmas gives them a chance, James. Not many others do

commentary: hard length, pushed into the covers. Could be tight, but Suryakumar doesn't collect cleanly...!
length ball wide of off stump, maybe a cutter. Yes, 125kph/77mph and toe-ended to backward point
pre_text: Here's Sanju (not that one): "Nothing guaranteed for India with so many Greens and Purples in the scorecard!"

commentary: short ball, climbing through over leg stump as Bethell pulls and misses. Too high
slotted over deep midwicket! Back-of-a-length offcutter, Bethell sizes it up and nails the flat pull
reverse-scooped into boards! Nonchalantly done by Bethell for another boundary, his sixth in 13 balls. On a length outside off and just helped away
pitched up and driven with an open face, couple to deep backward point
skips down and donks him for six! Round the wicket, into the arc as Banton advances, slides nicely on to the bat as he goes in to out over extra cover
pre_text: Axar Patel on

commentary: butchered, goes miles! SKY just frowns to himself. Fired in straight but Banton is on the charge and nails a 92-metre six over long-on!

Axar roars, you miss, I hit! Tossed up a bit higher, and it dips under the attempted slog-sweep to rock leg stump! Pace down to 84kph/52mph and Bantons loses his shape, loses his wicket. Now he wears the frown. England lose their fourth wicket inside eight overs
straight lines and nudged to leg
tries to reverse-pull his second ball, comes off bat and body but fails safely
slugged into the gap! Again the crowd goes silent... Touch short and Jacks is deep to haul this away through cow corner!
pre_text: Bhargav: "That's a poor shot from Benton.  After 2 sixes, you have to pick and choose balls which you want to hit.  Especially given they were 3 wickets down."

commentary: pushed through from over the wicket, Bethell smashes it through midwicket! Goes deep and bisects the boundary riders for another four
pre_text: Varun again

commentary: smeared over cover this time! Round the wicket, shortish into the pitch and Bethell makes room to clatter four more!
over again, zipped down on the stumps, jabbed through mid-on
95kph googly, shaves off stump! Tossed up outside the line and Jacks misses with an ungainly heave
connects this time, four through square leg! Length ball, sits up nicely and gets spanked off the back foot
fizzed down wide of off, swatted to long-off
loses his shape heaving to leg, comes off the hip to short fine leg
pre_text: Axar for a second

commentary: wide line, 92kph/57mph, plinked on the bounce out to deep point
Bethell cuts and misses, but it was pushed just beyond the off-side tramlines from round the wicket
fired wide, cut firmly to backward point, Bethell stutters and is well short as he dives... but Axar was stood back from the stumps and couldn't underarm it into the wicket!
angled into the pads as Jacks swings across the line. Somehow this deflects to backward point and they steal two
looped up wide of off, mistimed to cover
fired full on off and drilled to long-off. Second over without a boundary
Wide called for height. Bumrah not too pleased. Bounced on middle and leg, beat the pull
pre_text: Thanks Alan

commentary: Not sure how he got so much elevation on that chip-drive over cover point. Had pace to work with. Was a yorker just outside off
Under-edges a cut into the pitch that bounces over the bowler. Slow shortish ball wide of off
Low dipping full toss has been well negotiated with, brings up Bethell's fifty. Flicked through midwicket. Applause from the dugout
pre_text: Around

commentary: Another yorker, this one gets an 'ohhh' from the crowd. Bethell stays beside it and defends to cover. Thought of a single, not on
Slower one has been short-arm pulled, beats square leg to the right. No one in the deep. Back of length, angling in, Bethell getting it from just outside off
Full toss missed out. Was outside off, driven to cover
Wide on a back of length, cut to deep point
Reverse-sweeps it from down to low, gets it fine of short third. Picked it off a length after standing square-on, from outside off
Wide and full, driven hard and straight to sweeper cover
Shortish and wide, cut to deep cover. Axar fumbles but recovers quickly
Fullish and wide, guided to short third's left
Baby six over Kishan at deep midwicket. Quiet around the ground. Varun looks to close out the over by going full and flat on leg, Jacks doesn't pre-meditate and whips it without trying too hard
Full just outside off, slugged along the ground to deep midwicket
pre_text: Around

commentary: Surprised that's still inside the ground, hit the hoarding at the edge of the ground. Touch short, not much bounce, Jacks swivels and pulls it way over square leg. 95 metres to bring up England's 150
Misfield at cover. SKY the fielder. Was a wide ball on a length that was slapped hard
Wide on a length, looks to cut it hard. Under-edges it to point
They quiet down as the ball goes to ground and rolls to long-off. Wide on a length, Bethell lost his bottom hand after clearing the front leg and slapping it
pre_text: Chants getting louder by the minute

commentary: Fullish on off, whacked along the ground to long-on's left
Bethell almost outsmarted himself, then maintained balance to pick up four over short third. Made room and then got still, reached out with a check-cut. Was a slower one
pre_text: Arshdeep back

commentary: Follows him with an attempted yorker, the full ball is flicked over the infield and then to cow corner. Two well run

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Bethell, no run
commentary: Big cheer from the crowd. Bethell makes room, so Arshdeep bowls a full ball inches inside the wide tramline. Has to be let go
Low full toss on middle and leg has been whipped to the right of deep midwicket.
pre_text: "Arsh-deep Singh" chants now

commentary: Wide low full toss, Bethell looks to slap it through cover. Under-edges it into the crease and then towards point
Is that inside the cut strip? Seems so. Was a wide yorker that landed close to the return crease. Let go
Called wide, Arshdeep points towards the crease and says that landed well inside. Replay shows the yorker landed just outside off but passed the bat closer. Beats the cover drive
This is conclusively wide. Low full toss angling away, Jacks lets it pass

Another stunner from Axar, this one's a relay! Ran to the left from deep cover, then threw the ball to Dube coming in from the other side. Axar caught the ball while taking big steps, got over the boundary but only after one-hand throwing it. Every fielder sprints and swarms him. Was a wide, low full toss that Jacks slice-drove with decent timing.
dismissal: WG Jacks c Dube b Arshdeep Singh 35 (32m 20b 4x4 2x6) SR: 175

commentary: Gives it a bit of room and looks to cut hard. Gets a thickish edge wide of short third. Deep-backward point is fine
pre_text: Varun to close out

commentary: Cuffed wide of the bowler, too straight for long-off. Touch back of length if at all, and Bethell flat-bats it along the ground
This is survival bowling. Looks to hide it like a medium pacer, the back of lengther is left alone
Similar ball, cut to deep point
Fired fullish on middle, defended to the bowler
A bit too straight, quick enough for Curran to rock back and pull the shortish ball through deep square leg
Back of length just outside off, cut to long-off. 93ks
Slot ball actually but pacy at 141ks. Looks to punch it straight, inside edges it to point
pre_text: Arun: "this is game-on!.. 2 20  overs will seal the deal for England" But there are two Bumrah overs, one of them now. Wickets are premium now

commentary: Goes for the yorker, it's a full ball outside off. Bethell doesn't want to take it on. Square drives it towards deep point, can't get back for two
pre_text: Around

commentary: Another yorker missed, crowd stays quiet. SKY not happy with something, the line probably. On the legs and it's flicked behind square
Nails the yorker this time. Curran showed the full face and the ball went off the toe, to the bowler
pre_text: Square leg moves to short fine, fine leg moves to where the boundary was hit

commentary: Good slower bumper, grips and turns away. Curran was into the pull and then checked the shot to bunt it towards midwicket
pre_text: "Jasprit Bumrah" chants now

commentary: Wide and full, square driven to deep point. Applause from the crowd, end scene
Plan's obvious. Wide yorkers. This is well outside the tramline, let go
pre_text: Arshdeep to close out

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Bethell, no run
commentary: Almost a wicket! Plan's not to go wide this time. Reverse swinging yorker coming in. Line's perfect too, Arshdeep tries to nail middle stump. Jammed into the pitch.
Bethell wants to hit Arshdeep off that yorker length, so he shapes for the paddle. Has to reverse the shot last minute as the ball's wider than him. Guides it to backward point
pre_text: "Arshdeep Singh" chants back

commentary: Inswinging yorker on off, driven through point. Does well to bring back two
pre_text: Clapping build up from the crowd

commentary: Change up. Bouncer just outside off, pulled to long-on. Crowd's fully into it as Hardik stops and throws
Wide outside off. Yorker lands well outside off, Bethell lets it pass
Low full toss has been boshed over the bowler. Shushes the crowd. Cleared the front leg, held his shape and swung slightly across the line
Excellent ball dealt with in style! Near-perfect wide yorker, scratch the near, it was inside the tramline. Bethell reached out, opened the face and guided it through where first slip would've been
'Nothing you can do about it' yorker at the stumps, Curran jams it back to the bowler
pre_text: Bumrah, Hardik and Axar have an over. Bumrah will bowl out early. SKY wants wickets, esp of Bethell. Around the wicket

commentary: Another yorker, this is on middle, swiped across. Along the ground to long-on
Hat-trick of pinpoint yorkers, crowd recognise the genius. This was slow but looked quick at first glance. On middle and leg, worked to mid-on
Low full toss on leg, misses out. Curran flicked along the ground to deep midwicket's left
Low full toss on off, worked to long-on. England happy to try and see him off
Yep, safely negotiated. Full ball on leg is flicked to deep midwicket. Bumrah has his hands on his knees while looking on as the crowd applaud
pre_text: Can Bumrah get Bethell? Surely no big shot incoming

commentary: Almost a blinder but not to be. Bethell compiles a ton. Raises the bat, gets a bit of applause. Was a wide length ball, Hardik ran his fingers across it, Bethell stood tall and slapped it. Axar ran right from long-off and nearly took a one-hander
pre_text: Hardik to bowl the penultimate. England need 5-6 boundaries, India effectively need two wickets

commentary: Low full toss on off has been slugged flat to long-on. On the bounce

Taken on the midwicket boundary. Low full toss on leg stump, Curran did get under it but swayed the bat under it rather than muscle it. Tilak was on the boundary, stayed just inside while taking the catch high and looking back
pre_text: Ashu: ":( my heart is beating so fast." India taking time to set their field
dismissal: SM Curran c Tilak Varma b Pandya 18 (25m 14b 2x4 0x6) SR: 128.57

commentary: Full outside off, drilled to long-on. Change of strike, that was all that was needed
Near yorker, just a single. It's a very low full toss on off, Bethell looked to drive straight, got it to coveer
pre_text: Name chants continue

commentary: Nonchalant Hardik takes centre stage. Bowls a wide yorker a couple of inches inside the tramline. Overton lets it go, doesn't get a wide
pre_text: Effective free hit

commentary: That has to be the game! Bethell has tried to steal a second that was never on and is run out by miles! He buries his face in the ground and doesn't get up after the dive, not for a while at least. Was a near yorker on off that was driven flat to Hardik at long-off, good throw. On the bounce, to the keeper.
pre_text: No Axar, Dube it will be to bowl his first over. Fielding penalty will apply due to slow over rate

commentary: All but over, mathematically too. Attempted yorker, Archer looks to drive it straight. Inside edges it onto pad
Yorker outside off, jammed towards cover
Bashed over long-off, the chorus of Vande Mataram pauses for a second. Low full toss outside off, Archer stands still, follows through with a swipe
Wide well outside of off. Full ball is let go
Another six over long-off. Low full toss just outside off, Archer's front leg makes a bit of room and the bat comes down with might
Yorker has been munched over extra cover for six but it doesn't matter. Everyone stands and applauds, the crowd, superstars in the VIP boxes as the India players calmly celebrate
